evidence_items.source_quote: Polymerase chain reactions for Epstein-Barr virus, Herpes simplex virus, cytomegalovirus, and John Cunningham (JC) virus were negative.

rationale: 31-year-old male with HIV/AIDS and Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia who developed Wernicke encephalopathy. CSF PCR for cytomegalovirus was explicitly negative (E0_CONTRADICTED / C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Serological tests for campylobacter jejuni, EBV, cytomegalovirus, and mycoplasma pneumonae were negative.

rationale: 29-year-old primigravida diagnosed with Guillain-Barre syndrome in late pregnancy/postpartum. Serological testing for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: The detection of Cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein Barr virus (EBV), Adenovirus and Coxsackievirus were all negative (real-time PCR).
Rubella virus, CMV and EBV IgM antibody and DNA were later reported as negative.

rationale: 21-year-old male with HLH and Guillain-Barre syndrome secondary to Campylobacter jejuni infection. Both blood real-time PCR and CSF CMV IgM/DNA testing were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Searches for other pathogens, including Mycobacterium tuberculosis, atypical mycobacteria, cytomegalovirus, Cryptococcus and Aspergillus species, were negative.

rationale: 24-year-old woman with hypogammaglobulinemia post-rituximab who developed Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia and fatal EBV-positive DLBCL. BAL/microbiological workup for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Cytomegalovirus IgM test was positive.

rationale: 2-month-old male infant with white stools, cholestasis, and failure to thrive definitively diagnosed with Cystic Fibrosis (CFTR c.223C>T and exon 2-3 deletion; fecal elastase 0.6 ug/g). Serum CMV IgM was positive, which is only E3 supportive evidence subject to cross-reactivity, with negative TORCH and no confirmatory CMV PCR or organ diagnosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: CSF studies were negative for cryptococcal antigen, Lyme IgM antibody, Toxoplasmosis IgG antibody, varicella, VDRL, and CMV.

rationale: 70-year-old immunocompetent male with Cryptococcus gattii meningoencephalitis. CSF studies for CMV were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: CMV IgM antibody was negative; however, CMV IgG antibody was positive with reported value >10 (ref: 0.00-0.059).

rationale: 62-year-old male with COVID-19 pneumonia and acute EBV hepatitis (EBV VCA IgM+ and EBV PCR+). CMV IgM was negative; isolated CMV IgG positivity reflects past latent exposure rather than active CMV disease.

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood cultures, HBV, CMV-DNA, TORCH-IgM, G/GM, TB-IGRA, parasite antibody were negative.

rationale: 35-year-old male with primary intestinal extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma (EBV-positive) causing colonic perforations. CMV-DNA testing was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: The viral serology surveys including varicella zoster virus, herpes simplex virus, cytomegalovirus, and Japanese encephalitis virus were also negative.

rationale: 25-year-old man with acute meningoencephalitis and CLOCCs associated with Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection (IgM 1:320). Viral serology for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologic testing for acute or chronic infection with viral hepatitis types A, B and C, HIV, Epstein-Barr virus, Cytomegalovirus returned negative.

rationale: 28-year-old male with acute aflatoxicosis (AFB1 19.6 ppb) causing fulminant hepatic failure and rhabdomyolysis. Serologic testing for Cytomegalovirus returned negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Epstein-Barr (EB) virus IgM and cytomegalovirus (CMV) IgM were detected.

rationale: 4.5-year-old boy with recurrent lung infections and hematuria ultimately diagnosed with APDS1 (PIK3CD E1021K mutation). Serum CMV IgM and EBV IgM were detected, which is only E3 supportive evidence without confirmatory CMV PCR or organ-specific CMV diagnosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serological screening for congenital infections (i.e., Cytomegalovirus, Toxoplasma gondii, Varicella-Zoster Virus, and Hepatitis C Virus) during pregnancy and at birth (in the mother and her daughter) was negative, as was the proband neonatal extensive screening for inborn errors of metabolism.

rationale: 18-month-old girl with microcephaly and corpus callosum hypoplasia due to a novel TSC1 variant. Serological screening for congenital Cytomegalovirus during pregnancy and at birth was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Based on the historical, clinical, and laboratory data obtained, we initially considered intestinal perforation due to cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection as the probable etiology of peritonitis, and the differentials included, mycobacterial infections, fungal infections, neoplastic disease or Kaposi sarcoma.
Bowel perforation due to tuberculosis was confirmed as the final diagnosis

rationale: 26-year-old female with HIV and bowel perforations. CMV was initially considered as the probable etiology and treated empirically with 3 days of ganciclovir, but pathology confirmed intestinal tuberculosis as the final diagnosis (C2 competing diagnosis).

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood serology and PCR for EBV and cytomegalovirus (CMV) were negative.

rationale: Index patient (18-month-old boy) with BENTA/CARD11 mutation. Blood serology and PCR for cytomegalovirus were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Viral surveillance, including EBV, CMV, and HIV were negative.

rationale: 9-year-old Syrian boy with acquired TTP secondary to Brucella infection. Viral surveillance for CMV was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Tests for Cryptococcus antigen, Toxoplasmosis antigen, Ebstein Barr virus IgG and IgM, Cytomegalovirus IgG and IgM, Hepes Simplex virus polymerase chain reaction (PCR), Japanese encephalitis as well as cultures for tuberculosis and fungi (plasma and cerebrospinal fluid, CSF) were all negative.

rationale: 9-year-old boy with perinatal HIV and progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (JCV PCR+). Cytomegalovirus IgG and IgM tests were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Tests were negative for Pneumocystis jirovecii, acid fast bacilli, cytomegalovirus, parvovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, cryptococcus, histoplasmosis, syphilis, and influenza A.

rationale: 30-year-old female with HLH triggered by uncontrolled HIV. Testing for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Subsequent maternal serologic testing for herpes simplex, cytomegalic, and toxoplasmosis virus was negative.

rationale: 31-year-old primigravida with fetal hydrops/anemia caused by Parvovirus B19 (amniotic fluid PCR 2,589,801 copies/mL). Maternal serologic testing for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: The CSF culture results for possible organisms, such as human immunodeficiency virus, hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, bacteria, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, fungi, Borrelia, enteroviruses, Herpes viruses, and CMV, were negative.

rationale: 66-year-old man with myasthenia gravis, severe COVID-19, and critical illness polyneuropathy. CSF testing for CMV was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Cytomegalovirus immunoglobulin Ig G and IgM (negative), anti-streptolysin O titer (negative), hepatitis panel (negative), infectious mononucleosis screen (negative), EBV serology panel (negative).

rationale: 10-year-old girl with acalculous cholecystitis and rash due to Mycoplasma pneumoniae (IgM+). Cytomegalovirus IgG and IgM were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Viral serology was negative for cytomegalovirus, and aspergillus antigen was negative.

rationale: 13-year-old boy with generalized lymphatic anomaly who developed sirolimus-induced DIC. Viral serology for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Hepatophilic virus antibodies [anti-cytomegalovirus-immunoglobulin M (CMV-IgM), anti-Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-IgM, hepatitis A/B/C/E virus antibodies] and autoimmune liver disease antibodies were negative.

rationale: 5-year-4-month-old boy with STAT1 GOF mutation causing syndromic CMC and autoimmune diabetes. Anti-CMV IgM antibody was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Initial workup was negative for Epstein Bar Virus (EBV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), and Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection.

rationale: 60-year-old male with stage IV nongerminal center DLBCL. Initial workup was negative for cytomegalovirus infection (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Polymerase chain reaction found the patient to be reactive to cytomegalovirus (CMV), and Epstein Barr virus (EBV), but human herpes virus 8 was not detected.

rationale: 46-year-old man with multicentric Castleman disease and MSSA septic arthritis/osteomyelitis. Qualitative CMV PCR was reactive, which is E3 supportive only without viral load quantification, CMV end-organ syndrome, or CMV-directed therapy.

evidence_items.source_quote: Additional viral serology (adenovirus, coxsackievirus, echovirus, borrelia burgdorferi, cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, and parvovirus), immunological testing (systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, vasculitis, complement screening, and M-protein), a tuberculosis test and blood culture analyses were normal.

rationale: 52-year-old woman with recurrent hemopericardium caused by pericardial epithelioid angiosarcoma. Viral serology for cytomegalovirus was normal/negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: In the differential diagnosis, we excluded atopy, cystic fibrosis, immunodeficiency disorders, viral infections (with cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, and pneumotropic viruses), and fungal infections (Aspergillus sp. and Candida sp.).

rationale: 18-month-old female with plastic bronchitis following pneumonia after Glenn procedure. Cytomegalovirus infection was excluded in the differential diagnosis (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Laboratory workup was all negative and included Lyme, Toxoplasma, QuantiFERON, Syphilis, COVID-19, Herpes simplex virus, Herpes zoster virus, Varicella-zoster virus, Epstein-Barr virus, Bartonella, Cytomegalovirus, liver function tests, basic metabolic panel, thyroid panel, vitamin B1, B12, folic acid, rheumatoid factors (RF), antinuclear antibodies (ANA), antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA), and angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE).

rationale: 69-year-old man with heart transplant diagnosed with sirolimus-induced toxic optic neuropathy. Laboratory workup for Cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Microbiological serology was negative for hepatitis A, B, C, and E, as well as CMV, VZV, Q fever, and toxoplasmosis.

rationale: 24-year-old male with acute cholestatic liver injury associated with khat chewing. Microbiological serology for CMV was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Her serological test results revealed positivity for Mycoplasma pneumoniae [M. pneumoniae; immunoglobulin G = 1,810.79 (<100.00) 103U/L and immunoglobulin M = 3,381.64 (<770.00) 103U/L] but negativity for Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, and hepatitis A, B, and C.

rationale: 4-year-old girl with Kawasaki disease, cholestatic hepatitis, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection. Serological testing for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: EBV, CMV and HSV 1 serologies show acquired immunity, HIV and HSV 2 serologies were negative.

rationale: 66-year-old man with metastatic prostate cancer who developed fatal fulminant hepatitis attributed to abiraterone acetate. CMV serology showed acquired immunity (past latent exposure only, not active CMV disease).

evidence_items.source_quote: Laboratory work up revealed pancytopenia, high HIV viral load, elevated sedimentation rate, positive cytomegalovirus (CMV) immunoglobulin G (IgG) and ParvoB19 IgG, and negative CMV and Parvo B19 DNA polymerase chain reaction (Table 1).
evidence_items.test_name: Serum CMV IgG and CMV DNA PCR

rationale: 28-year-old male with AIDS diagnosed with HHV-8-associated multicentric Castleman disease. CMV DNA PCR was negative; CMV IgG positivity reflects past latent exposure only (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Immunohistochemical staining demonstrated negativity for CD117, SMA, CMV, and HSV-2.

rationale: 42-year-old man with isolated colonic Langerhans cell histiocytosis. Immunohistochemical staining of the colonic polyp was negative for CMV (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Meningitis/encephalitis panel (PCR testing for Escherichia coli K1, Haemophilus influenzae, Listeria monocytogenes, Neisseria meningitidis (encapsulated), Streptococcus agalactiae, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Cytomegalovirus, Enterovirus, Herpes Simplex virus 1 and 2, Human Herpesvirus 6, Human Parecho virus, Varicella zoster virus, Cryptococcus neoformans/gattii) was negative.

rationale: 55-year-old man with pembrolizumab-associated encephalopathy. CSF meningitis/encephalitis PCR panel was negative for Cytomegalovirus (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: PCR for HSV 1-2, varicella-zoster virus, Epstein-Barr virus, adenovirus, parvovirus B19, Enterovirus, cytomegalovirus, and Borrelia burgdorferi was negative.

rationale: 48-year-old man with primary angiitis of the CNS treated with intracranial stenting. CSF PCR for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: The neutrophil count was normal (5.3 x 109/L, reference range 2.0-10.0 x 109/L) as were serum brain natriuretic peptide (44 pg/mL, reference range <100 pg/mL), lactate dehydrogenase (116 units/L, reference range: 98-192 units/L), urine Streptococcus pneumoniae and Legionella pneumophila antigen tests, and cytomegalovirus IgG and IgM serologies.

rationale: 83-year-old man with CLL who developed chlorambucil-induced acute interstitial pneumonitis. Cytomegalovirus IgG and IgM serologies were normal/negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: No abnormalities were observed in the CSF bacteriological tests, CSF Gram stain, and CSF virus tests (herpes simplex virus, varicella-zoster virus, enterovirus, cytomegalovirus, rubella virus, and Epstein-Barr virus).

Serology for syphilis, hepatitis B, mycoplasma, human immunodeficiency virus antibody, herpes simplex virus, hepatitis C virus antibody, varicella, cytomegalovirus, mumps, measles, and Epstein-Barr virus was negative.

rationale: 26-year-old female with anti-NMDAR/mGluR5 autoimmune encephalitis and bilateral ovarian teratoma. Both CSF viral testing and serum serology for cytomegalovirus were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) of the CSF was negative for cytomegalovirus (CMV), Cryptococcus neoformans, Escherichia coli, Enterovirus, Haemophilus influenzae B, human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6), human parechovirus, herpes simplex virus (HSV) 1/2, Listeria monocytogenes, Neisseria meningitidis, Streptococcus agalactiae (group B streptococcus (GBS)), Streptococcus pneumoniae, and varicella zoster virus (VZV).

rationale: 2-year-8-month-old girl with extrapontine myelinolysis following extreme hypernatremia. Multiplex CSF PCR for CMV was negative and CSF CMV antibody specificity index was normal (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Surprisingly CMV IgG Ab was >10.0 U/mL (N < 0.59 U/mL) and CMV IgM Ab was markedly elevated at 233.0 AU/mL (N < 29.9 AU/mL) consistent with SLE and acute CMV infection.

rationale: 60-year-old female with SLE and acute STEMI. Elevated CMV IgM (233.0 AU/mL) and CMV IgG (>10.0 U/mL) were reported, which constitute E3 supportive serology only (subject to cross-reactivity in active SLE) without CMV PCR, viral load, or end-organ CMV confirmation.

evidence_items.source_quote: Among microbiology and virology analysis performed, IgM Cytomegalovirus-antibodies (with negative antigenemia) and IgM Epstein-Barr virus antibodies (with not significant PCR amplification) were found.

rationale: 58-year-old woman with Bartonella henselae infection mimicking vasculitis, resolved with azithromycin. Although CMV IgM was detected (E3), CMV antigenemia was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Increased levels of Ig G herpes virus type I-II, Ig G cytomegalovirus, Ig G Epstein-Barr virus, and Ig G rubella virus were determined.

rationale: 1-year-old girl with chromosome 22q11.2 deletion syndrome. Isolated CMV IgG elevation reflects past/maternal exposure rather than active CMV disease (E0_CONTRADICTED).

evidence_items.source_quote: CMV, head ultrasound and MRI were also negative.

rationale: Neonate with congenital Zika syndrome (placental Zika RNA+). Workup for microcephaly was negative for CMV (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Human cytomegalovirus IgG and rubella virus IgG antibodies were positive.

rationale: 21-year-old woman with autoimmune GFAP astrocytopathy. Human CMV IgG positivity reflects past latent exposure only, and CSF viral PCR was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood works including an ANA, anti-Jo-1, anti-Ro, anti-La, anti-RNP/Smith, serum myoglobin, aldolase, CMV/EBV titers, and anti-histone antibodies were all negative.

rationale: 21-year-old male with NXP-2 positive dermatomyositis. CMV titers were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: However, in our patient, there were no proven infectious complications during the hospital stay or later apart from EBV reactivation.

rationale: 66-year-old man post-allo-HSCT who developed late EBV-related PTLD. Donor and recipient were CMV-seropositive pre-transplant (latent status), and the report explicitly states no proven infectious complications occurred apart from EBV reactivation.

evidence_items.source_quote: The serum IgM test for toxoplasma, rubella virus, cytomegalovirus, herpes simplex virus and parvovirus B19 (TORCH) was negative.

rationale: 55-year-old woman with CML who developed EBV-positive lymphomatoid granulomatosis. Serum CMV IgM (TORCH) and plasma CMV testing were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood and urine cultures, as well as viral panel testing for cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), human herpes virus 6 (HHV6), HIV, parvovirus B19 (PVB19), hepatitis C virus (HCV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis A virus (HAV), and herpes simplex virus (HSV), were negative, as were screening examinations for autoimmune and rheumatoid markers.

rationale: 15-year-old boy with pre-B-ALL complicated by disseminated juvenile xanthogranuloma and HLH. Viral panel testing for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: A repeat lumbar puncture showed an OP of 22 cmH2O and CSF analyses were unrevealing (i.e. meningitis panel, cryptococcal, lyme, West Nile virus, arbovirus, CMV, Herpes simplex virus (HSV), VDRL, gram stain, cultures, IgG index, myelin basic protein, angiotensin-converting enzyme, and oligoclonal bands), except for a mildly elevated protein of 70 mg/dL (similar to prior results at the outside hospital).

rationale: 60-year-old man with biopsy-confirmed toxic spongiform leukoencephalopathy. Both serum infectious workup and CSF analysis for CMV were unrevealing/negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Microscopy from blood cultures and urine cultures was negative, and CMV and EBV viraemias remained very low level.

rationale: 30-year-old renal transplant recipient with severe COVID-19 hyperinflammation treated with IV anakinra. CMV viremia remained very low level (E3 supportive only without CMV end-organ syndrome or CMV-directed therapy).

evidence_items.source_quote: Viral markers (HAV, HBV, HCV, CMV, and EBV) were negative, while ANA and ASMA were positive (1 : 320 with homogeneus pattern and 1 : 80, resp.).

rationale: 72-year-old woman with type 1 autoimmune hepatitis who developed drug-induced ischemic pancolitis. Viral markers for CMV were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologic tests were negative for Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), and hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection.

rationale: 9-year-old boy with Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease and encephalopathy. Serologic tests for cytomegalovirus were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: EBV, CMV, and HBV serum tests were negative.

rationale: 7-year-old girl with Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease and encephalopathy. Serum tests for CMV were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: CMV level on PCR was undetectable.

rationale: 35-year-old male renal transplant recipient with acute esophageal necrosis (black esophagus) post-revascularization. CMV level on PCR was undetectable (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Tests for CMV, HIV, HSV and syphilis were negative while serologic tests for Toxoplasma gondii were positive
A mild persistent EBV viremia (up to 2.58log10) and an intermittent CMV viremia (< 3.08log10) was observed.

rationale: Mother and child with APDS2 (PIK3R1 mutation) and toxoplasmosis. Child tested negative for CMV; mother had low-level intermittent CMV viremia (<3.08 log10) without CMV end-organ disease or CMV-directed therapy (E3 supportive only).

evidence_items.source_quote: The plasma and pericardial fluid were negative for Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, parvovirus B19, enterovirus, and adenovirus via polymerase chain reaction.
evidence_items.test_name: Plasma and pericardial fluid CMV PCR

rationale: 62-year-old male with pre-B cell ALL who developed nilotinib-induced pericardial effusion. Plasma and pericardial fluid PCR for cytomegalovirus were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Prior to alloHSCT, the patient was EBV-IgG and CMV-IgG seropositive; he received peripheral blood stem cells collected from an unrelated HLA-matched donor (10/10, MUD) who was EBV-IgG seronegative and CMV-IgG seropositive.

rationale: 52-year-old man with AML post-alloHSCT who developed EBV-related PTLD. Pre-transplant donor and recipient CMV-IgG seropositivity reflects past latent exposure only, not active CMV disease.

evidence_items.source_quote: CSF polymerase chain reaction (PCR) panel [herpes, chickenpox, cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), enterovirus, para-echo, mumps, and rubella], gram/Zn stain, bacterial antigen latex agglutination, and cultures were negative.

rationale: 11-year-old girl with MR vaccine-associated MOG-antibody positive ADEM with optic neuritis. CSF PCR panel was negative for cytomegalovirus (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: PCR analysis of the CSF did not detect EBV, CMV, HSV, VZV, enterovirus, M. tuberculosis, or fungal pathogens.

rationale: 30-year-old man with relapsing Susac syndrome. CSF PCR analysis did not detect CMV (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Her infectious work-up returned negative.

rationale: 21-year-old woman with acute fatty liver of pregnancy in the second trimester. Infectious work-up including viral studies for Cytomegalovirus returned negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: The results of the serological tests were negative for cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, Toxoplasma, and Brucella.

rationale: 8-year-old girl with pediatric autoimmune hepatitis presenting with erythema nodosum. Serological testing for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) and BK viral markers were negative.

rationale: 30-year-old male renal transplant recipient with SARS-CoV-2 infection. Cytomegalovirus viral markers were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Viral serology for CMV, BKV was negative and the result of urine examination was normal.

rationale: 35-year-old male renal transplant recipient with SARS-CoV-2 infection. Viral serology for CMV was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: He had previous chronic hepatitis B, legionellosis, chronic Q fever and cytomegalovirus infection.

rationale: 58-year-old male renal transplant recipient with relapsing visceral leishmaniasis. Cytomegalovirus infection is mentioned only as a previous historical comorbidity with no active CMV episode or diagnostic evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: He had cerebral toxoplasmosis, chronic hepatitis B, gastrointestinal CMV infection, and anal squamous cell carcinoma.

rationale: 75-year-old male with HIV and relapsing visceral leishmaniasis. Gastrointestinal CMV infection is listed only as past medical history without active CMV testing or episode during the reported course.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serological tests for acute hepatitis A, B, C and E, Epstein-Barr virus and cytomegalovirus infection were negative.

rationale: 51-year-old man with acute cholestatic hepatitis due to Artemisia annua herbal tea. Serological tests for cytomegalovirus infection were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Culture and microscopy of sputum and BAL materials were negative for fungi, bacteria, acid-fast bacilli, Pneumocystis carinii and cytomegalovirus.

rationale: 49-year-old female with AML who developed cryptogenic organizing pneumonia. Culture and microscopy of sputum and BAL were negative for cytomegalovirus (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Viral markers tested at 17 months after transplantation were HBsAg/sAb/cAb (-/+/+), anti-HCV(+) and CMV Ab IgG/IgM (+/-).

rationale: 52-year-old female renal transplant recipient with chronic hepatitis C. CMV Ab IgG/IgM was (+/-), indicating negative IgM and past latent IgG exposure only (E0_CONTRADICTED).

evidence_items.source_quote: Viral markers tested at 36 months following transplantation were HBsAg/sAb/cAb (-/-/+), anti-HCV (+) and CMV Ab IgG/IgM (+/+).

rationale: 53-year-old male kidney transplant recipient with chronic hepatitis C. CMV Ab IgG/IgM was (+/+), which is E3 supportive serology only without CMV PCR, viral load, antigenemia, or CMV end-organ disease.

evidence_items.source_quote: High amounts of EBV DNA were detected in saliva as well as dental plaques, whereas cytomegalovirus (CMV) DNA was undetectable in respective samples.
evidence_items.test_name: Saliva and dental plaque CMV DNA

rationale: 24-year-old woman with CD70 deficiency and chronic EBV infection. Cytomegalovirus DNA was undetectable in saliva and dental plaque samples (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood and urine cultures as well as viral studies (including parainfluenza, influenza, pneumoviruses, adenoviruses, bocaviruses, rhinovirus, herpex, human herpesvirus-7 [HHV-7], cytomegalovirus [CMV], and varicella-zoster) were negative.

rationale: 17-day-old newborn with severe AKI, TMA/ATIN, and multi-organ failure. Viral studies for cytomegalovirus were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Since she had a history of herpetic keratitis, we suspected recurrent herpetic keratitis, yet polymerase chain reaction test results of anterior-chamber aqueous humor samples for herpes simplex virus, varicella-zoster virus, and cytomegalovirus were all negative.

rationale: 75-year-old female with recurrent Candida fungal keratitis post-amniotic membrane transplantation. Aqueous humor PCR for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: No DNA of herpes simplex virus, Epstein-Barr virus, or human cytomegalovirus was detected.

rationale: 48-year-old man with anti-CASPR2 autoimmune encephalitis mimicking cerebral infarction. No DNA of human cytomegalovirus was detected in CSF (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Furthermore, cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) as well as hemochromatosis, Wilson disease, and alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency were excluded.

rationale: 54-year-old female with acute liver failure induced by metamizole. Cytomegalovirus was excluded (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Immunoglobulin M (IgM) antibodies for herpes simplex virus, Epstein-Barr virus, and cytomegalovirus were negative.

rationale: 31-year-old man with AML who developed VZV meningoencephalitis and meningomyelitis. IgM antibodies for cytomegalovirus were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: The screening for toxoplasmosis, rubella, cytomegalovirus, and herpes simplex virus infections was negative.
Deoxyribonucleic acid detection of Epstein-Barr virus and human cytomegalovirus were both negative.

rationale: Male patient with benign recurrent intrahepatic cholestasis type 1 (ATP8B1 variant). Screening and DNA detection for human cytomegalovirus were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Laboratory studies were negative for toxoplasmosis, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, HIV, CMV, VDRL, and Brucella agglutination, while EBV-IgM showed a borderline positive result.

rationale: 32-year-old woman with Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease. Laboratory studies for CMV were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Tests for Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, hepatitis and human immunodeficiency viruses were negative.

rationale: 75-year-old woman with acute myeloid leukemia presenting as acute liver failure. Tests for cytomegalovirus were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Quantitative detection of CMV- PP65 antigen and CMV- DNA was also negative.
evidence_items.test_name: CMV pp65 antigen and CMV DNA

rationale: Chinese Milroy disease family case. Quantitative detection of CMV pp65 antigen and CMV DNA was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Tests for mycoplasma, herpes simplex virus, varicella-zoster virus, and cytomegalovirus antibodies were also negative.

rationale: 15-year-old female with post-COVID-19 ischemic stroke. Tests for cytomegalovirus antibodies were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Serological tests for common infectious agents, including human T-cell lymphotropic viruses I and II; hepatitis A, B, and C viruses; human immunodeficiency viruses 1 and 2; herpes simplex viruses 1 and 2; Epstein-Barr virus; cytomegalovirus; rubella, measles, mumps, and poliomyelitis viruses; as well as Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Chlamydia spp., Yersinia spp., Campylobacter spp., Rickettsia spp., Borrelia spp., pathogens of toxoplasmosis and cryptococcosis, and Coxiella burnetii, were negative.

rationale: 18-year-old pregnant woman with ADEM. Serological tests for cytomegalovirus were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Immunoreactivity for Cytomegalovirus (CMV) was negative.

rationale: 75-year-old male on hemodialysis with ulcerative pancolitis treated with vedolizumab. Colonic biopsy immunoreactivity for Cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologic tests for Parvovirus B19, EBV, CMV, and Waaler-Rose test, were consistent with prior infection or non-immunized state.

rationale: 14-year-old girl with autoimmune hemolytic anemia and heterozygous ADA mutation. Serologic tests for CMV were consistent with prior infection or non-immunized state only (no active CMV disease).

evidence_items.source_quote: QuantiFERON  blood tests were negative, and tests for Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, toxoplasma, syphilis, hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, and human immunodeficiency virus were all negative.

rationale: 61-year-old man with isolated neurosarcoidosis. Tests for cytomegalovirus were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, West Nile virus, and rheumatoid factor were not present.

rationale: 75-year-old male with Lyme neuroborreliosis. Cytomegalovirus was not present (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Anti-CMV, anti-EBNA-1, and anti-VCA (IgM) were also negative.
Serum PCR detected HHV-6 (no CMV or EBV).

rationale: 12-year-old girl with sulfasalazine-induced hypersensitivity syndrome. Both anti-CMV serology and serum CMV PCR were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Microbiological cultures of the lavage did not reveal bacterial or fungal growth and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for cytomegalovirus DNA was also negative.

rationale: 47-year-old heart transplant recipient with HSV-1 pneumonia and refractory bronchospasm. BAL PCR for cytomegalovirus DNA was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Other than an initially positive CMV viral load (440 copies/ml, age 1 year, treated with ganciclovir for 90 days), his first laboratory workup was unremarkable.

rationale: 7-year-old boy with LIG4 deficiency. Reports a historical low-level CMV viral load (440 copies/mL) at age 1 year treated with ganciclovir without end-organ CMV syndrome, and unremarkable subsequent workup (historical/E3 only).

evidence_items.source_quote: serologic tests for HepA, HepB, HepC, CMV, and EBV came back negative.

rationale: Teenage twin girls with LIG4 deficiency, bone marrow failure, and sclerosing cholangitis. Serologic tests for CMV were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Screening for cytomegalovirus, toxoplasma, human immunodeficiency virus, vasculitis and thrombophilia were all negative.

rationale: 21-year-old man with branch retinal artery occlusion due to patent foramen ovale. Screening for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: CMV IgG was reactive, CMV IgM non reactive.

rationale: 36-year-old male with malignant rhabdoid tumor of the lung. CMV IgG was reactive and CMV IgM was nonreactive, reflecting past latent exposure only (E0_CONTRADICTED).

evidence_items.source_quote: Mycophenolate was discontinued suspecting CMV ileitis. CMV PCR was sent.

rationale: 68-year-old male liver transplant recipient with severe lactic acidosis. CMV ileitis was suspected in the differential diagnosis and CMV PCR was sent, but laparotomy and biopsy confirmed monomorphic Burkitt lymphoma (C2 competing diagnosis).

evidence_items.source_quote: Serological tests for HIV, cytomegalovirus (CMV), herpes virus, and rubella virus were negative.

rationale: 8-month-old boy with CD40LG mutation and Talaromyces marneffei bloodstream infection. Serological test for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: PCR and serology for Bartonella, Brucella, Borrelia, Toxoplasma, CMV, and Francisella were performed, all resulting negative.

rationale: 4-year-old boy with Kawasaki disease presenting with retropharyngeal involvement. PCR and serology for CMV were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: No other abnormal laboratory results were found (serology for CMV, EBV, HIV, HBV, HCV, Toxoplasma, Treponema pallidum, Leishmania, Coxiella burnetii, Mycoplasma pneumonia, Chlamydia pneumonia, Quantiferon test, RF, IgA, IgG, IgM, C3, C4, ANA, and ENA Screen).

rationale: 27-year-old male with lymphomatoid papulosis type A. Serology for CMV was normal/negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Additional workup including CMV, Brucella, Q fever serologies, Toxoplasma IgG antibody and urine histoplasma antigen were negative, and a low detectable EBV viral load (1080 copies/ml) was regarded as an incidental finding.

rationale: 76-year-old man with splenic infarction, B-cell lymphoma, and secondary HLH. CMV serology was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Other viruses including cytomegalovirus and polyoma (BK) virus were not detected.

rationale: 18-year-old male with collapsing glomerulopathy and parvovirus B19 viremia undergoing kidney transplantation. Cytomegalovirus was not detected (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: HIV load in CSF was 2 x 104 c/ml, while PCR based testing for JC Virus (JCV), Herpes Simplex Virus 1/2 (HSV 1/2), Varicella Zoster Virus (VZV) and Cytomegalovirus (CMV) were negative.

rationale: 48-year-old male with HIV and neurosyphilis. CSF PCR testing for Cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: The remaining microbiological studies (cytomegalovirus polymerase chain reaction in peripheral blood and the auramine and Ziehl-Neelsen staining as well as the bacteriological and mycological cultures of the bronchial culture and bronchoalveolar lavage [BAL]), taken within the first 48 hours of admission, were negative.

rationale: 68-year-old man with myeloproliferative neoplasm who developed hydroxyurea-induced pneumopathy. Peripheral blood CMV PCR was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Serum antibodies against herpes simplex, varicella-zoster, Epstein-Barr, and mumps viruses, cytomegalovirus, and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) were not elevated.

rationale: 62-year-old man with acute autonomic, sensory, and motor neuropathy associated with meningoencephalitis. Serum antibodies against cytomegalovirus were not elevated (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: The bronchoalveolar (BAL) fluid was positive for cytomegalovirus (CMV), human herpes virus 6 (HHV-6), and Actinomyces odontolyticus using next-generation sequencing.

rationale: 17-year-old female post-HSCT with a right upper lobe pulmonary mass ultimately confirmed as Coprinopsis cinerea fungal infection on lung tissue resection/NGS/histology. BAL fluid NGS was qualitatively positive for CMV without quantitative viral load or CMV histopathology in the lung lesion (E3 supportive only; C2 competing diagnosis).

evidence_items.source_quote: HBsAg (hepatitis B surface antigen) and anti-HCV (hepatitis C virus) antibody were negative, HIV serology was non-reactive and his serum was negative for Cytomegalovirus DNA.

rationale: 30-year-old renal transplant recipient with disseminated tuberculosis. Serum was negative for Cytomegalovirus DNA (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Antibody titers for herpes simplex, varicella, cytomegalovirus, toxoplasma and rubella were conducted and found to be normal.

rationale: 25-year-old pregnant woman on olanzapine whose infant had microcephaly and bilateral anophthalmos. Antibody titers for cytomegalovirus were normal/negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: A thrombophilia panel, antiphospholipid panel, cytomegalovirus and toxoplasmosis antibodies, and neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia panel were ordered and were negative.

rationale: 25-year-old pregnant woman with in utero fetal stroke caused by congenital HSV-2 infection. Cytomegalovirus antibodies were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: All his blood cultures were negative, serologic testing for cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, and parvovirus B-19 were negative for acute or past infection.

rationale: 4-year-old boy with Kawasaki disease and Yersinia enterocolitica infection. Serologic testing for cytomegalovirus was negative for acute or past infection (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Both viral and bacterial infections including Epstein Barr Virus (EBV), Cytomegalovirus (CMV) and Mycoplasma pneumonia were negative.

rationale: 18-month-old child with co-amoxiclav-induced Stevens-Johnson syndrome. Testing for Cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: The recipient was cytomegalovirus-seropositive and toxoplasma-seropositive and had a body mass index of 24.5 kg/m2.

rationale: 64-year-old male liver transplant recipient who developed fatal GVHD. Pre-transplant recipient CMV seropositivity reflects latent exposure only, and no infectious agents were identified in tissue/marrow samples.

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient's plasma level of antibodies was negative for numerous pathogens (aerobic and anaerobic bacteria, Mycoplasma tuberculosis, Toxoplasma gondii, Ebstein-Barr virus, Cytomegalovirus, hepatic viruses, Chlamydia trachomatis, yersinia enterocolica, Candida etc).

rationale: 15-year-old male with pericarditis and cardiac tamponade complicating appendicitis. Plasma antibodies were negative for Cytomegalovirus (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Other potential viral antibodies, including coxsackievirus, cytomegalovirus, parainfluenza virus, human herpes virus, and Epstein-Barr virus, were also tested, but the results returned negative.

rationale: 34-year-old pregnant woman with fulminant type 1 diabetes following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Viral antibodies for cytomegalovirus returned negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologies for HIV, EBV, and CMV were all negative, as was a skin prick allergy test.

rationale: 6-year-old boy with DOCK8 deficiency. Serology for CMV was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Serological evaluation for infection was remarkable for equivocal Lyme ELISA but negative Lyme western blot, negative blood and gonococcal cultures, negative interferon-gamma release assay for tuberculosis, negative Babesia, malaria antigen, anaplasma, chlamydia/gonorrhea nucleic acid, negative hepatitis B core Ab, surface antigen, and hepatitis C viral Ab, nonreactive HIV, negative HSV IgM by immunofluorescence assay, cytomegalovirus (CMV) viral load, and CMV Ab.
evidence_items.test_name: CMV viral load and CMV Ab

rationale: 63-year-old man with adalimumab-associated CNS sarcoidosis. Cytomegalovirus viral load and CMV antibody were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: infection indexes (procalcitonin, bacterial and fungal culture of bone marrow, and examinations of Cytomegalovirus and Epstein-Barr virus) and serum tumor markers were normal.

rationale: 24-year-old female with macrophage activation syndrome secondary to nodular panniculitis. Examinations of Cytomegalovirus were normal/negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: TORCH tests were performed in the first trimester, and the results were negative, including toxoplasmosis, rubella, cytomegalovirus, and herpes simplex virus.

rationale: 24-year-old pregnant woman with Listeria monocytogenes infection in twin pregnancy. TORCH testing for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: CSF studies, performed as described elsewhere, for Cytomegalovirus (CMV) PCR, HSV PCR, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), JC virus (JCV) PCR,  cryptococcal antigen, fungal culture, acid-fast stain and culture, and VDRL were  all negative.

rationale: 59-year-old female with CLL on alemtuzumab who developed fatal disseminated strongyloidiasis. CSF Cytomegalovirus PCR was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Sputum gram stain and culture, sputum fungal culture, respiratory influenza nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT), respiratory viral NAAT, serum cytomegalovirus NAAT, Pneumocystis jiroveci direct fluorescent antibody, and serum Aspergillus galactomannan antigen were all negative.

rationale: 44-year-old woman with antisynthetase syndrome who developed peripheral T-cell lymphoma causing hypoxemic respiratory failure. Serum cytomegalovirus NAAT was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: The virology screening included Epstein Barr virus (EBV) and Cytomegalovirus (CMV) was negative.

rationale: 40-year-old man with alopecia universalis and ulcerative colitis. Virology screening for Cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: The tests for Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), herpes simplex virus (HSV), varicella-zoster virus, and adenovirus were negative.

rationale: 56-year-old woman with autoimmune hepatitis and false-positive HAV-IgM. Tests for cytomegalovirus were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: There was no evidence of infection with cytomegalovirus, HIV virus, herpes simplex virus, or Epstein-Barr virus.

rationale: 66-year-old female with chronic hepatitis B who developed entecavir-associated thrombocytopenia. There was no evidence of infection with cytomegalovirus (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: In serological tests, VZV-IgG, EBV-VCA-IgG, and CMV-IgG were avidite positive;

rationale: 6-year-old boy with NF1 and benign neurofibroma. CMV-IgG avidity positivity reflects past latent exposure only, not active CMV disease (E0_CONTRADICTED).

evidence_items.source_quote: Anti-CMV IgM and anti-parvovirus B19 IgM antibodies were detected.

rationale: 7-year-old boy with cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa. Anti-CMV IgM (alongside anti-parvovirus B19 IgM) was detected, which is E3 supportive serology only without CMV PCR, viral load, or CMV diagnosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: TORCH titers revealed high IgG levels of rubella and cytomegalovirus.

rationale: 1-month-old neonate with cholestatic jaundice caused by Enterobacter cloacae UTI. High CMV IgG levels reflect maternal/past exposure only, not active CMV disease (E0_CONTRADICTED).

evidence_items.source_quote: Viral serology markers (cytomegalovirus IgG and IgM, parvovirus IgG and IgM) were negative in the maternal blood, and no viral genome was isolated in her amniotic fluid or the fetal ascites sample.
evidence_items.test_name: Maternal CMV serology and amniotic fluid PCR

rationale: 28-year-old pregnant woman with fetal ascites due to ductal plate malformation. Maternal CMV IgG/IgM were negative and no viral genome was isolated from amniotic fluid or fetal ascites (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: PCRs for HSV, EBV, and CMV were negative.

rationale: Boy with chr7p22/chr15q11 deletion immunodeficiency and cerebral vasculitis. Extended septic workup excluded cytomegalovirus and CSF CMV PCR was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Additional laboratory examinations yielded no evidence of hepatitis A, B or C, cytomegalovirus or Epstein-Barr virus infection.

rationale: 62-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis who developed injectable gold-induced hepatitis and neutropenia. Laboratory workup yielded no evidence of cytomegalovirus infection (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Hepatitis A, B, C, and CMV as well as autoimmune panel for anti-mitocondrial and anti-smooth muscle antibodies were all negative.
CMV, Gram stains, PAS and AFB stains were negative.

rationale: 49-year-old male with HIV and stage IVb classical Hodgkin lymphoma involving the liver. Blood CMV testing and liver biopsy CMV staining were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Infectious balance is negative (blood cultures, serology of atypical germs, PCR of Herpes viridae, Herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV1), Herpes simplex virus 2(HSV2), Parvovirus, varicella zoster virus (VZV), cytomegalovirus (CMV) , Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) , Human Herpesvirus (HHV6) and (HHV8), Sputum stain for Koch bacillus (BK) and gene-expert are negatives, coprocultures and PCR of gastrointestinal tract are negatives).

rationale: 28-year-old woman with macrophage activation syndrome revealing Hodgkin lymphoma. CMV PCR was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: CSF testing was negative for human cytomegalovirus (HCMV), herpes simplex virus (HSV), and varicella zoster virus (VZV) by polymerase chain reaction (PCR).

rationale: 76-year-old male with glioblastoma mimicking viral encephalitis. CSF PCR for human cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Tests for other viral (CMV, EBV, VZV, HSV, dengue), fungal (Histoplasma, Cryptococcus), bacterial (Bartonella, Rickettsia, Legionella, Mycobacterium) and parasitic (Leishmania, Toxocara) pathogens were negative.

rationale: 14-year-old male with WHIM syndrome and ocular toxoplasmosis. Tests for CMV were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: The mother was tested negative for toxoplasma, CMV, herpes, and rubella.

rationale: 35-year-old pregnant woman with fetal 11q22.3-q23.3 deletion. Maternal testing for CMV was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: During the first trimester of pregnancy, his mother had been infected by a cytomegalovirus (CMV). As a consequence, at birth he suffered a thrombocytopenia purpura leading to a diffuse cerebral hematoma, which was resorbed after several weeks. Also due to CMV infection, B.L. was diagnosed with a profound and bilateral deafness at 6 months of age.

rationale: 17-year-old boy with ASD and profound deafness participating in a facilitated communication accelerometry study. Congenital CMV infection is mentioned only as historical past etiology from birth/infancy, with no active CMV disease or diagnostic testing in the current episode.

evidence_items.source_quote: The following investigations were either normal or negative: blood cultures for bacteria, viruses, and fungi along with serology for Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, human immunodeficiency virus, hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, antinuclear antibody test, and rheumatoid factor.

rationale: 32-year-old male with Kikuchi disease, Hashimoto hypothyroidism, and medullary thyroid microcarcinoma. Serology for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Immunostains for HSV-1/2, CMV, and EBV are also negative.

rationale: 25-year-old male with relapsing polychondritis and meningoencephalitis. Brain biopsy immunostains for CMV were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Serology for CMV, EBV, Lyme, and Treponema pallidum and thyroperoxidase, thyroglobulin, antinuclear, anti-extractable nuclear antigen, anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic, lupus anticoagulant, aquaporin-4 (AQP4), myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG) and paraneoplastic antibodies were within normal limits or negative.

rationale: 54-year-old female with spinal cord ischemia related to thoracic disc herniation. Serology for CMV was normal/negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: She was tested for infectious diseases (Epstein Barr virus, Cytomegalovirus, Human Immunodeficiency virus, Hepatitis B and C virus, Toxoplasmosis, Syphilis, Parvovirus and Herpes Simplex virus 1/2), autoimmune diseases, blood, urine and stool cultures.

rationale: 71-year-old woman with biopsy-proven IgA vasculitis. Cytomegalovirus was tested as part of the infectious workup with no positive CMV finding reported and IgA vasculitis established as final diagnosis (C2 competing diagnosis).

evidence_items.source_quote: The serological tests for HIV, syphilis, cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), and Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) were negative, except for anti-EBV, anti-CMV, and anti-MP IgG.

rationale: 57-year-old man with post-COVID-19 Guillain-Barre syndrome. Only anti-CMV IgG was positive (past latent exposure), with negative acute CMV serology (E0_CONTRADICTED).

evidence_items.source_quote: To rule out further differential diagnoses, virological testing was performed, showing no abnormalities; in particular, an cytomegalovirus polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test in the blood was negative.

rationale: 23-year-old male with Crohn disease and infliximab-induced lupus-like syndrome. Blood CMV PCR test was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: The workup for sepsis, including testing for bacterial and fungal cultures, mycoplasma, chlamydia, legionella, tubercle bacillus, virus like cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, and novel coronavirus was negative.

rationale: 36-year-old male with adenovirus pneumonia and multisite embolism. Sepsis workup for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: He tested negative for CMV and HSV, but Lyme serology was found to be positive (total IgM and IgG antibodies).

rationale: 69-year-old male with Lyme neuroborreliosis and SIADH. Testing for CMV was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis of the CSF was negative for JCV, HSV RNA, cytomegalovirus RNA, herpes virus Type 6 (HVT6) DNA and VZV DNA.

rationale: 50-year-old male with CLL who developed PML (JCV DNA+ on brain biopsy). CSF PCR was negative for cytomegalovirus RNA (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Antibodies to HSV1, HSV2, CMV, EBV, HBV, VZV, HCV and HIV in serum and cerebrospinal fluid, as well as sarcoidosis and tumor markers in serum revealed no abnormality.

rationale: 50-year-old woman with neuromyelitis optica and autoimmune thyroiditis. Serum and CSF CMV antibodies revealed no abnormality (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Epstein-Barr virus DNA, cytomegalovirus DNA, purified protein derivative test and blood culture were negative.

rationale: Child with TBL1XR1-RARB positive acute promyelocytic leukemia. Cytomegalovirus DNA was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Laboratory studies showed elevated titers of the anti-Toxoplasma, anti-Herpes simplex virus IgG, anti-Herpes simplex virus IgM, and anti-cytomegalovirus IgG antibodies, as well as low cell lymphocyte and CD4-positive lymphocyte counts.
Although the vitreous fluid sample was subjected to broad-range PCR, multiplex PCR, and other culture tests, no positive results were obtained.

rationale: 64-year-old man on prednisolone with bilateral endogenous Candida albicans subretinal abscesses. Anti-CMV IgG antibody positivity reflects past latent exposure only, vitreous multiplex PCR was negative, and empirical valganciclovir failed (E0_CONTRADICTED / C2 competing diagnosis).

evidence_items.source_quote: Also, lactate dehydrogenase (395 U/l), muscle enzymes (creatine phosphate kinase 75 IU/l, CK-MB 10 IU/l), thyroid hormones (free thyroxine 10.98 pmol/l, thyroid-stimulating hormone 1.925 muIU/ml), celiac serology, cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, herpesvirus serology and autoantibodies (ANA, nDNA, ANCA) were normal, and megacolon was excluded using barium enema.

rationale: 8-year-old boy with functional aerophagia. Cytomegalovirus serology was normal/negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Immunohistochemistry for CMV was negative.

rationale: 61-year-old female with Crohn disease who developed disseminated HSV-2 colitis and perforation. Immunohistochemistry of the subtotal colectomy specimen was negative for CMV (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Once again, an infectious workup, including stool adenovirus, cytomegalovirus, norovirus, enterovirus, cryptosporidium, giardia, clostridium difficile, Escherichia coli and other bacterial stool pathogens were negative.

rationale: 13-year-old boy with Hoyeraal-Hreidarsson syndrome and colonic angioectasia. Stool infectious workup was negative for cytomegalovirus (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Maternal prenatal tests showed blood type A, Rh +, negative maternal serum indirect Coombs test, immunity to rubella and negative serology results for toxoplasma, hepatitis surface antigen and cytomegalovirus.

rationale: Female newborn with perinatal-lethal Gaucher disease presenting as hydrops fetalis. Maternal prenatal serology was negative for cytomegalovirus (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: There were no significant changes in serum or CSF antibodies for HIV, herpes simplex virus, Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, varicella-zoster virus, Japanese encephalitis A and B virus, and JC virus.

rationale: 48-year-old woman with multiple system atrophy and opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome. Serum and CSF antibodies for cytomegalovirus showed no significant changes/were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Because the patient presented with a fever, infectious disease panels were performed including IgM and IgG antibodies against Cytomegalovirus, rubella virus infection, Treponema pallidum, anti-Epstein-Barr virus-IgG and IgM, hepatitis B and C, and tropical diseases (thick drop test). He was also tested for central nervous system infections using cerebrospinal fluid analysis. All panels and tests were negative.

rationale: 56-year-old man with renal intravascular large B-cell lymphoma. IgM and IgG antibodies against Cytomegalovirus were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Viral hepatitis A, B and C markers were negative as well as IgM antibodies for EBV, CMV and HSV.

rationale: 34-year-old woman post-liver transplant with de novo autoimmune hepatitis. IgM antibodies for CMV were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: While tuberculosis PCR, virology (including herpes simplex, varicella-zoster, cytomegalovirus, and JC virus), syphilis, toxoplasma serology, cryptococcal antigen, bacterial, and fungal cultures were negative in blood and CSF.

rationale: 22-year-old female with HIV who developed EBV encephalitis (CSF EBV 42,864 copies/mL). Virology for cytomegalovirus was negative in blood and CSF (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Serology tests were negative for Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), Cytomegalovirus (CMV), human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and viral hepatitis B and C.

rationale: 37-year-old man with acute myocarditis following BNT162b2 vaccine. Serology tests for Cytomegalovirus were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: All viral screens including atypical viruses such as Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), and herpes simplex virus (HSV) were found to be negative.

rationale: 54-year-old male with buccal SCC on cisplatin/radiotherapy who developed acute occult hepatitis C. Viral screens for cytomegalovirus were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: The serologic tests for EBV, CMV, and chronic viral hepatitis including HCV were unremarkable.

rationale: 42-year-old male with disseminated gastric MALT lymphoma. Serologic tests for CMV were unremarkable/negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Auto-immune (complement, cryoglobulinemia, rheumatoid factor, anti-glomerular basement membrane, anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic, antinuclear antibodies) and viral [hepatitis C and B, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), cytomegalovirus, parvovirus B19, Human Herpesvirus (HHV)-6 and -8, human immunodeficiency virus and syphilis] tests were negative.

rationale: 28-year-old woman with TAFRO syndrome. Viral tests including cytomegalovirus were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood and CSF examination showed no evidence of bacterial and viral infection including syphilis, mycobacteria, borrelia, EBV, CMV, HTLV, and herpes type-6.

rationale: 49-year-old woman with nonceliac gluten sensitivity. Blood and CSF examination showed no evidence of CMV infection (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Serological investigations showed no evidence of active Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), cytomegalovirus disease (CMV), herpes simplex, leptospira, tuberculosis, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, VDRL, and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV);

rationale: 23-year-old pregnant woman with SLE and HLH. Serological investigations showed no evidence of active CMV disease (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Serology tests for cytomegalovirus, toxoplasmosis, parvovirus B19, tuberculosis, and rheumatologic tests including angiotensin-converting enzyme, antinuclear antibody, and antiphospholipid antibodies were negative.

rationale: 11-year-old girl with Behcet disease. Serology tests for cytomegalovirus were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Ig M to cytomegalovirus (CMV) was negative, and Ig G to CMV was positive.

rationale: 21-year-old woman with severe chronic active EBV infection. CMV IgM was negative and CMV IgG was positive, reflecting past latent exposure only (E0_CONTRADICTED).

evidence_items.source_quote: Serological assays showed positive results for IgM antibodies to Parainfluenza virus, but negative results for antibodies to respiratory syncytial virus, influenza virus (types A and B), cytomegalovirus (CMV), Adenovirus, Legionella pneumophila, Mycoplasma pneumonia, Chlamydia pneumoniae, Q-rickettsia, and Cryptococcus neoformans.

rationale: 27-year-old female renal transplant recipient with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia. Serology for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Tests for pathogens that included Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), cryptococcus, tuberculosis, and parasites were negative; blood cultures for bacteria, acid-fast bacilli, and fungi were also negative.

rationale: 23-year-old male with NK/T cell lymphoma. Tests for cytomegalovirus were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Additionally, we tested him for beta-D-glucan, Aspergillus galactomannan antigen, cytomegalovirus antigen, and anti-glycopeptidolipid-core IgA for Mycobacterium avium and performed interferon-gamma release assay; however, these tests were negative.

rationale: 62-year-old man with systemic AL amyloidosis. Cytomegalovirus antigen test was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Hepatotropic viruses, adenovirus, CMV, HIV, EBV, Coxiella burnetii, Yersinia enterocolitica, and Entamoeba histolytica were negative.

rationale: 35-year-old woman with Legionella pneumophila pneumonia and eosinophilic gastroenteritis. Serology for CMV was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Tests for viral hepatitis A, B, C and E, as well as cytomegalovirus were negative.

rationale: 53-year-old woman with pembrolizumab-induced immune-related hepatitis. Tests for cytomegalovirus were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: The cytomegalovirus IgG and Epstein-Barr virus IgG were positive, but IgM was negative for both.

rationale: 11-year-old girl with brucellosis causing bone marrow aplasia. CMV IgG was positive and CMV IgM was negative, reflecting past latent exposure only (E0_CONTRADICTED).

evidence_items.source_quote: Serology for Influenza A and B, parvovirus B19, EBV, and CMV, ECHO virus, Coxsackie virus, HSV, VSV, and adenovirus, Coxiella burnetii, Chlamydia, Leptospira spp., and Mycoplasma pneumoniae were negative.

rationale: 21-year-old man with Brucella melitensis myocarditis. Serology for CMV was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Laboratory examinations including serologic tests for acute EBV and CMV viral infections were negative.

rationale: 54-year-old male with AIDS and pericardial Kaposi sarcoma. Serologic tests for acute CMV viral infection were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: The PCR was positive for HSV I and negative for HSV II, cytomegalovirus, and varicella zoster virus.

rationale: 57-year-old male with HSV-1 linear endotheliitis post-keratoplasty. Aqueous humor PCR was negative for cytomegalovirus (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV) and cytomegalovirus (CMV) tests were negative.

rationale: 26-year-old woman with Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease. Cytomegalovirus tests were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Extensive workup for bacterial, fungal, viral, and autoimmune etiologies was negative during this hospitalization, as well as subsequent hospitalizations. CSF studies included basic studies (Table 1) as well as testing for acid-fast bacilli stain, anaerobic culture, Aspergillus galactomannan, cryptococcal antigen, cytomegalovirus, enterovirus, fungal culture, group B Escherichia coli, Haemophilus influenza type B, herpes simplex virus 1 and 2, JC virus, Listeria antibody, multiple sclerosis IgG synthetic rate, Streptococcus pneumonia antigen, Tropheryma whippelii, varicella zoster, venereal disease research lab test (VDRL), and 14-3-3 protein.

rationale: 63-year-old male with chronic autoimmune meningoencephalitis responding to anakinra. CSF testing for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Viral serologies including HIV, hepatitis A, B, C; EBV, CMV, dengue, and leptospira were negative.

rationale: 53-year-old man with Q fever (Coxiella burnetii). Viral serology for CMV was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Similarly, norovirus, astrovirus, and cytomegalovirus infection were ruled out.

rationale: 70-year-old female with IBD-like colitis following CAR T-cell therapy. Cytomegalovirus infection was ruled out (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Normal serological tests, IgE of 564 UI/ml (nl = 87 UI/ml), fast glucose of 54 mg/dl and negative autoimmune disease factors except for antinucleus factor, which was positive (1/40).

rationale: 30-year-old female with enlarged vestibular aqueduct syndrome. Serological tests including cytomegalovirus were normal/negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood, urine, and cerebrospinal fluid cultures showed no growth, and cerebrospinal fluid polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for enterovirus, herpes simplex virus type 1 and 2, varicella zoster virus, cytomegalovirus, measles, human herpes virus-6, and adenovirus was negative.

rationale: 3-year-old girl with adenoviral pneumonia and acute encephalopathy. CSF PCR for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Lumbar puncture was negative for syphilis, toxoplasmosis, Cryptococcus, Cytomegalovirus and Epstein-Barr Virus.

rationale: 34-year-old man with HIV-associated vacuolar myelopathy. Lumbar puncture was negative for Cytomegalovirus (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Cytomegalovirus DNA and IgM antibody were negative on multiple blood tests.
In addition, cytomegalic inclusion body was not present in the tissue sample from endoscopic biopsy.

rationale: Brucellosis case; CMV DNA and IgM antibody were negative on multiple blood tests and no cytomegalic inclusions were seen on endoscopic biopsy (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Serological tests failed to show infection by common agents such as HIV, syphilis, viral hepatitis, cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, and Toxoplasma spp.

rationale: Gleich's syndrome and urticarial vasculitis; serological tests failed to show CMV infection (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Dermatology department was consulted, and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for herpes simplex viruses 1 and 2, Varicella zoster virus, Epstein barr virus, and Cytomegalovirus, in addition to HIV serology and VDRL, were performed, with negative results.

rationale: Invasive aspergillosis; PCR for Cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: The immediate posttransplant period was complicated with acute cellular grade Ia kidney rejection (treated with three bolus of MPN), and a biopsy confirmed Herpes simplex virus (HSV) and cytomegalovirus (CMV) esophagitis (treated with acyclovir and ganciclovir, respectively).

rationale: Simultaneous pancreas-kidney transplant recipient presenting 19 years post-transplant with graft plasmacytoma-like PTLD; biopsy-confirmed CMV esophagitis occurred in the immediate posttransplant period 19 years earlier (historical past, not current episode).

evidence_items.source_quote: Parameters suggestive of autoimmune or viral hepatitis, such as cytomegalovirus antibody, Epstein-Barr virus, antinuclear antibodies, antimitochondrial antibodies, hepatitis B surface antigen, and hepatitis C virus antibodies, were negative.

rationale: PFIC-3 (ABCB4 deficiency); cytomegalovirus antibody was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Also, acute infection with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and cytomegaly virus (CMV) was ruled out.

rationale: Exertional heat stroke with acute hepatic failure; acute CMV infection was ruled out (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Polymerase chain reaction [PCR] assays of CSF for influenza virus, herpes simplex virus 1 and 2, adenovirus, enterovirus, cytomegalovirus, human herpesvirus- 6, epstein-barr virus, and varicella zoster virus were all negative.

rationale: Influenza A H1N1 cerebellitis; both CSF PCR and blood serology were negative for cytomegalovirus (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: He subsequently had bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) which returned negative for mycobacterium, fungus, legionella and cytomegalovirus on culture.

rationale: Pulmonary carcinosarcoma with aspergillosis; BAL culture was negative for cytomegalovirus (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologic tests for varicella virus, human herpes virus type 1-2-6-8, coxsackie virus, adenovirus, cytomegalovirus, Toxoplasma gondii, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, and Borrelia burgdorferi resulted negative, as well as the antistreptolysin title and oropharyngeal swab.

rationale: Ceftriaxone-induced hepatitis with acute EBV infection; serologic test for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) IgG and IgM was also negative.

rationale: Cetuximab-induced esophageal ulcer; CMV IgG and IgM were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and cytomegalovirus (CMV) real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) tests were negative.

rationale: BCG-triggered HLH in CYBB chronic granulomatous disease; CMV real-time PCR was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Serology tests for syphilis, cytomegalovirus (CMV) and HIV were all negative.

rationale: Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome; serology test for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: A shell vial culture system, coupled with monoclonal antibody-based detection, was used for the isolation of cytomegalovirus.
Results of all microbiologic investigations were negative.

rationale: SARS-CoV pneumonia; shell vial culture for cytomegalovirus and all microbiologic investigations were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologies of CMV and rubella showed an old immunization.

rationale: Griscelli syndrome type 2 with macrophage activation syndrome; CMV serology showed only an old immunization (E0 contradicted).

evidence_items.source_quote: In addition to routine blood test and urine cultures, the histories of infection were collected (e.g., HCV, HBV, tuberculosis, cytomegalovirus, parvovirus, varicella-zoster virus, HIV, EBV).

rationale: EBV-related B-cell lymphoproliferative disorder; infectious workup including cytomegalovirus was negative except for anti-EBV IgG (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: BAL samples were sent for culture and for nucleic acid testing for Legionella, Chlamydia, Cytomegalovirus, influenza virus, and Pneumocystis Carinii, together with nasopharyngeal swabs for influenza RT-PCR.

rationale: H1N1 ARDS; BAL nucleic acid testing for Cytomegalovirus was performed, H1N1 was confirmed, and no CMV infection was found (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: CMV was excluded by negative early antigenemia assay, polymerase chain reaction and shell vial culture.
evidence_items.test_name: CMV antigenemia, PCR, shell vial culture

rationale: Chronic GVHD post-BMT; CMV was excluded by negative early antigenemia assay, PCR, and shell vial culture (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, influenza, parainfluenza, human metapneumovirus, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), Ebstein-Barr virus (EBV), and cytomegalovirus (CMV) were negative.

rationale: Sarcoidosis ARDS; viral respiratory panel was negative for cytomegalovirus (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: EIA values for IgG antibodies was positive against VZV, HSV-1 and CMV in both serum and CSF (table 3).

rationale: 79-year-old woman with VZV myelitis; CMV IgG was positive in serum and CSF while IgM was negative, reflecting latent seropositivity rather than active CMV disease (E0 contradicted).

evidence_items.source_quote: The EIA value for IgG antibody was positive for VZV, HSV-1 and CMV in both serum and CSF (table 3).

rationale: 73-year-old man with VZV myelitis; CMV IgG was positive in serum and CSF with negative IgM, reflecting latent seropositivity without active CMV infection (E0 contradicted).

evidence_items.source_quote: Serum immunoglobulin (Ig)-G and M antibodies against herpes simplex virus (HSV) 1 and 2, varicella zoster virus (VZV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), rubella, and toxoplasma were normal except for high anti-rubella IgG and anti-CMV IgG.

rationale: Bilateral acute depigmentation of iris; only anti-CMV IgG was elevated with normal IgM, indicating past latent exposure rather than acute CMV disease (E0 contradicted).

evidence_items.source_quote: PCR was negative for HSV, EBV, and CMV and positive for VZV.
Blood PCRs were positive with high levels of VZV and low levels of CMV. The CMV viremia was attributed to secondary reactivation due to her severely immunosuppressed state.

rationale: Disseminated VZV acute liver failure; liver biopsy PCR was negative for CMV, and low-level blood CMV PCR was attributed to secondary reactivation without CMV end-organ disease (E3 supportive / no end-organ disease).

evidence_items.source_quote: The IgG antibodies of Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and Human Cytomegalovirus (CMV) were positive, while the IgM antibodies and the test of the nucleic acid of EBV and CMV were negative.
evidence_items.test_name: CMV IgM and nucleic acid test

evidence_items.source_quote: The test of the nucleic acid of CMV and EBV in CSF was negative.

rationale: Streptococcus suis and cryptococcal meningitis in HIV; CMV IgG was positive while IgM and blood/CSF nucleic acid tests for CMV were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Other causes for a vasculitis were excluded, like the presence of cryoglobulins or a hepatitis (screening assays for Hepatitides B and C, CMV, EBV, and HIV were negative).

rationale: PTU-induced Churg-Strauss syndrome; screening assay for CMV was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: He developed low-level cytomegalovirus (CMV)-viremia (Table 1) and leukopenia 4-months after transplantation, and his MPA was discontinued and the valganciclovir (VGCV) dose increased from 450 to 900 mg daily for treatment.

rationale: Renal transplant recipient presenting 9 months post-transplant with fever, AKI, and proteinuria; low-level CMV viremia occurred 4 months post-transplant and resolved within 4 weeks (historical past, E3 low-level).

evidence_items.source_quote: Serological tests for Epstein-Barr, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, cytomegalovirus, toxoplasma, and Brucella spp were all negative.

rationale: Isolated neurosarcoidosis; serological test for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Cytomegalovirus and cryptococcus serology were both negative.

rationale: Hodgkin lymphoma; cytomegalovirus serology was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Results of virology PCR for CMV, EBV, and adenovirus were negative.

rationale: Bronchogenic cyst in a 28-month-old girl; virology PCR for CMV was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient was tested for toxoplasmosis, hepatitis B and C viruses, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), syphilis, cytomegalovirus (CMV), and Epstein-Barr virus, which were negative.

rationale: Adult-onset Still's disease post-ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 vaccine; testing for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Empiric ganciclovir was started; however it was discontinued once CMV colitis was ruled out by serology, quantitative polymerase chain reaction, and immunohistochemistry studies.

rationale: Ulcerative colitis; empiric ganciclovir was discontinued once CMV colitis was ruled out by serology, quantitative PCR, and immunohistochemistry (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: CMV DNA was undetectable.

rationale: Primary hypoadrenalism with acute intermittent porphyria; CMV DNA was undetectable (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: CSF cultures for bacteria, fungi, and other viruses and peripheral blood examination for cytomegalovirus were negative.

rationale: HHV-6B encephalitis post-OLT; peripheral blood examination for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Hepatitis A, B, and C virus infections were ruled out serologically as well as CMV, HIV, and Leptospira infections.

rationale: Severe dengue with portal vein thrombosis; CMV infection was ruled out serologically (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Additionally, tests for human immunodeficiency virus, Hepatitis B virus (HBV), Hepatitis C virus, Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, and parvovirus B19 were negative.

rationale: ITP post-Moderna SARS-CoV-2 vaccine; test for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Head CT showed periventricular calcifications, likely consistent with earlier infarction and ventricular asymmetry, but cytomegalovirus, toxoplasmosis, and brain MRI/MRA were unremarkable.

rationale: Hepatocerebral POLG-related mtDNA depletion syndrome; cytomegalovirus testing was unremarkable (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Histopathology was negative for CMV colitis.

rationale: CLL presenting with chronic diarrhea; colonic histopathology was negative for CMV colitis (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Cerebrospinal fluid study (CSF) showed lymphocytic pleocytosis (WBC: 12, lymphocyte 98%) with normal protein and glucose, and viral serology for HSV1, HSV2, CMV, EBV, VZV, mumps, adenovirus, enterovirus, and parechovirus were negative.

rationale: CLIPPERS; CSF viral serology for CMV was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: No viral infections could be detected (serology for hepatitis A-B-C, cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, and human immunodeficiency virus was negative).

rationale: Familial Mediterranean fever with steatohepatitis; serology for cytomegalovirus was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Allo-HSCT was performed with reduced intensity conditioning (RIC) regimen with fludarabine, treosulfan, and anti-thymocyte globulin (ATG), before transplant with a matched unrelated donor (MUD), with both recipient and donor being positive for Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and cytomegalovirus (CMV) IgG.

rationale: Autoimmune limbic encephalitis post-allo-HSCT; recipient and donor were pre-transplant CMV IgG positive, and investigations for underlying viral causes were negative (E0 contradicted).

evidence_items.source_quote: Testing for SARS-CoV-2, CMV and HSV infections were negative at time of fetal death.

rationale: Stillbirth due to umbilical cord aneurysmal thrombosis and Factor V Leiden; testing for CMV infection was negative at time of fetal death (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Other biochemical parameters, cystic fibrosis gene, cationic trypsinogen, trypsin inhibitor gene mutations were normal, viral panel (CMV, rubella, EBV, toxoplasma, hepatitis A,B), ANA, ANCA, ASCA autoantibodies and PPD test were negative.

rationale: Autoimmune pancreatitis with Crohn's disease; viral panel for CMV was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: The CSF virology assessment for HSV PCR and IgM antibodies against herpes simplex, cytomegalovirus, Japanese encephalitis, varicella zoster virus, dengue and Epstein Barr virus was negative.

rationale: Paraneoplastic brachial plexopathy from lung malignancy; CSF IgM antibodies against cytomegalovirus were negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: Cytomegalovirus PCR, herpes PCR (type 1/2), mycobacterium PCR were negative in CSF; also, no growth was noted in fungal culture.

rationale: Toxoplasma encephalitis post-HSCT; CSF Cytomegalovirus PCR was negative (C1 refutation).

evidence_items.source_quote: She had high transaminases enzyme without proof of cytomegalovirus (CMV), HSV-1, HSV-2 syphilis, and tuberculosis infection.

rationale: Acute necrotizing encephalopathy of childhood; high transaminases without proof of cytomegalovirus infection (C1 refutation).
